                document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function() {
                    // Run bv-ads script first
                    (function initAds() {

    const container = document.querySelector('.bv-content-wrapper');

    if (!container) { return; }
    if (!container.classList.contains('bv-content-wrapper--with-ads')) { return; }

    const ads = {
        sky: {
            left: {
                id: 'sidebar-ad-left-sky',
                html: '<div id="sidebar-ad-left-sky" class="bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--left bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--sky"></div>'
            },
            right: {
                id: 'sidebar-ad-right-sky',
                html: '<div id="sidebar-ad-right-sky" class="bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--right bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--sky"></div>'
            }
        },
        half: {
            left: {
                id: 'sidebar-ad-left-half',
                html: '<div id="sidebar-ad-left-half" class="bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--left bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--half"></div>'
            },
            right: {
                id: 'sidebar-ad-right-half',
                html: '<div id="sidebar-ad-right-half" class="bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--right bv-content-wrapper__ad-placement--half"></div>'
            }
        }
    };

    function insertIfMissing( ad ) {
        if ( !document.getElementById( ad.id ) ) {
            container.insertAdjacentHTML( 'afterbegin', ad.html );
        }
    }

    function removeIfPresent( id ) {
        document.getElementById( id )?.remove();
    }

    function insertPair( pair ) {
        insertIfMissing( pair.left );
        insertIfMissing( pair.right );
    }

    function removePair( pair ) {
        removeIfPresent( pair.left.id );
        removeIfPresent( pair.right.id );
    }

    // Keep these in sync with @bp-ad-step-1 / @bp-ad-step-2 in mediawiki.skin.variables.less
    const skyQuery = window.matchMedia( '(min-width: 1320px)' );
    const halfQuery = window.matchMedia( '(min-width: 1700px)' );

    const handler = () => {
        if ( halfQuery.matches ) {
            removePair( ads.sky );
            insertPair( ads.half );
        } else if ( skyQuery.matches ) {
            removePair( ads.half );
            insertPair( ads.sky );
        } else {
            removePair( ads.sky );
            removePair( ads.half );
        }
    };

    skyQuery.addEventListener( 'change', handler );
    halfQuery.addEventListener( 'change', handler );
    handler();

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Publish the sticky footer ad's height as --bv-footer-ad-height.
    //
    // Anything docked to the bottom of the viewport - notably Raptive's
    // collapsed video player, see Tweaks.less - has to clear this unit. Its
    // height is not a constant: AdThrive_Footer_1 is served at several creative
    // sizes (320x50, 320x100, 728x90 and others), so a hardcoded offset clears
    // whichever fill it was measured against and overlaps the rest. Measure it.
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

    // AdThrive's own footer wrapper is the element it pins to the viewport:
    // `AdThrive_Footer_1_phone` on mobile, `_desktop` on wider viewports. Prefer
    // it over the GAM iframe container, which is nested inside it, is not always
    // present, and measures only the creative rather than the wrapper.
    const footerAdSelectors = [
        '[id^="AdThrive_Footer"]',
        '[id^="google_ads_iframe_"][id*="AdThrive_Footer"]'
    ];

    const root = document.documentElement;

    function findFooterAd() {
        for ( const selector of footerAdSelectors ) {
            const el = document.querySelector( selector );
            if ( el ) { return el; }
        }
        return null;
    }

    function publishFooterAdHeight( el ) {
        const height = el ? Math.round( el.getBoundingClientRect().height ) : 0;
        root.style.setProperty( '--bv-footer-ad-height', height + 'px' );
    }

    // Measure the fixed wrapper AdThrive pins to the viewport rather than the ad
    // container inside it, so any padding or chrome on the wrapper is included.
    function footerAdBox( el ) {
        let node = el;
        while ( node && node !== document.body ) {
            if ( getComputedStyle( node ).position === 'fixed' ) { return node; }
            node = node.parentElement;
        }
        return el;
    }

    let footerAdSizeObserver = null;

    function watchFooterAd() {
        const el = findFooterAd();
        if ( !el || footerAdSizeObserver ) { return false; }

        const box = footerAdBox( el );

Muted</div></div></div></div></div></div><h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Deck">Deck</span></h2>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Deck" title="Deck">Deck</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>Both players in a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">Pokémon Trading Card Game</a> require a playing <b>Deck</b>. An official deck is either purchased or built with 60 cards, composed of <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon cards</a>, <a href="#Energy_card">Energy cards</a>, and <a href="#Trainer_card">Trainer cards</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Booster_pack">Booster pack</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Booster_pack_(TCG)" title="Booster pack (TCG)">Booster pack (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p><b>Booster packs</b> are currently packs of 10 cards from a given <a href="#Expansion">Expansion</a>. Boosters offer the chance to acquire stronger cards to strengthen a <a href="#Theme_Deck">Theme Deck</a>, create new decks of cards, or customize old ones. Every booster pack is guaranteed to contain at least one <i>Rare</i> (<span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Rarity" title="Rare"><img alt="Rare" src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/b/b9/Rarity_Rare.png/21px-Rarity_Rare.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="21" height="20" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/b/b9/Rarity_Rare.png/31px-Rarity_Rare.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/b/b9/Rarity_Rare.png/42px-Rarity_Rare.png 2x" data-file-width="3611" data-file-height="3461"></a></span>) card, with generally three <i>Uncommon</i> (<span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Rarity" title="Uncommon"><img alt="Uncommon" src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/0/0f/Rarity_Uncommon.png/21px-Rarity_Uncommon.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="21" height="20" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/0/0f/Rarity_Uncommon.png/31px-Rarity_Uncommon.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/0/0f/Rarity_Uncommon.png/42px-Rarity_Uncommon.png 2x" data-file-width="3611" data-file-height="3461"></a></span>) cards and the remainder being <i>Common</i> (<span class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/Rarity" title="Common"><img alt="Common" src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8c/Rarity_Common.png/21px-Rarity_Common.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="21" height="20" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8c/Rarity_Common.png/31px-Rarity_Common.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/8/8c/Rarity_Common.png/42px-Rarity_Common.png 2x" data-file-width="3611" data-file-height="3461"></a></span>). Since the release of the <a href="/wiki/Legendary_Collection_(TCG)" title="Legendary Collection (TCG)">Legendary Collection</a> set, one <i><a href="#Holofoil_card">reverse Holofoil</a></i> print of a common, uncommon, or rare card has also been included in every pack.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Constructed_Deck">Constructed Deck</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Deck#Constructed_Deck" title="Deck">Deck → Constructed Deck</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>A <b>Constructed Deck</b> (also referred to as <i>Full Deck</i>) is a 60-card deck built by a player from that player's own <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">Pokémon Trading Card Game</a> collection.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_1_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px; align-content: start;" data-google-query-id="CJH9_M_G9pYDFSYirAAd3KAO6Q"><div id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0__container__" style="border: 0pt;"><iframe id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" name="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" title="3rd party ad content" width="1" height="1" scrolling="no" marginwidth="0" marginheight="0" frameborder="0" aria-label="Advertisement" tabindex="0" allow="private-state-token-redemption" data-load-complete="true" data-google-container-id="1" style="border: 0px; vertical-align: bottom;"></iframe></div></div><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Deck_archetype">Deck archetype</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Deck_archetype_(TCG)" title="Deck archetype (TCG)">Deck archetype (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>A <b>Deck archetype</b> is a player <a href="#Constructed_Deck">Constructed Deck</a> utilizing a set structure or theme (a certain <a href="#Pokémon_type">Pokémon type</a> and/or <a href="#Energy_card">Energy type</a>, specific <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon cards</a> and/or <a href="#Trainer_card">Trainer cards</a>, etc.).  Various players often have slight differences between their own decks of the same archetype.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Expansion">Expansion</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game_expansions" title="List of Pokémon Trading Card Game expansions">List of Pokémon Trading Card Game expansions</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>After the release of the original <a href="/wiki/Base_Set_(TCG)" title="Base Set (TCG)">Base Set</a> in 1996/1999, each subsequent release of <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon card</a> sets has been known as an <b>Expansion</b> set. Typically four expansions are released per year. They become <a href="#Standard_format">Standard</a> and <a href="#Expanded_format">Expanded</a> format legal two weeks after they are released in the United States. Expansions are grouped into a <a href="#Series">series</a> often taking its title from the first expansion in that given grouping (itself typically based off of the title of a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_games" title="Pokémon games">video game</a> release), such as the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game#HeartGold_&_SoulSilver_Series" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">HeartGold & SoulSilver Series</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game#Black_&_White_Series" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">Black & White Series</a>, or the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game#XY_Series" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">XY Series</a>.  Players who have collected all of the cards released in a given Expansion are considered to have a <i>Complete set</i>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Half_Deck">Half Deck</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Half_Deck_(TCG)" title="Half Deck (TCG)">Half Deck (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>The <b>Half Deck</b> is popular among many <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">Pokémon Trading Card Game</a> players, particularly in Japan. In Half Deck play, both players use a 30-card deck instead of a traditional 60-card one and lays out three <a href="#Prize_Card">Prize cards</a> instead of six.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Promotional_card">Promotional card</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Promotional_cards_(TCG)" title="Promotional cards (TCG)">Promotional cards (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>Unlike regular <a href="#Expansion">Expansion sets</a> and <a href="#Booster_pack">Booster packs</a>, <b>Promotional cards</b> are not available for purchase in stores. They are given way as special gifts.
A great many Promotional card sets have been produced over the years for the Pokémon Trading Card Game.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Preconstructed_Deck">Preconstructed Deck</span></h3>
<p>See <i><a href="#Theme_Deck">Theme Deck</a></i> or <i><a href="#Trainer_kit">Trainer kit</a></i> below.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Theme_Deck">Theme Deck</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Theme_Deck_(TCG)" title="Theme Deck (TCG)">Theme Deck (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>A <b>Theme Deck</b> is a <i>Preconstructed</i> 60-card deck that is sold pre-packaged (also referred to as <i>Full Deck</i>). Most Theme Decks are designed with a <a href="#Deck_archetype">specific strategy</a> (such as <a href="#Special_Conditions">Special Conditions</a>) or theme (such as <a href="/wiki/First_partner_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="First partner Pokémon">first partner Pokémon</a>) in mind. They tend not to be as strong as player <a href="#Constructed_Deck">Constructed Decks</a>, but can otherwise be a sound introduction to the game for new players since they have all the cards necessary for a single player to begin playing immediately. Theme Decks are also a defined gameplay category in the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game_Online" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game Online">Pokémon Trading Card Game Online</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Trainer_kit">Trainer kit</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Deck#Trainer_kit" title="Deck">Deck → Trainer kit</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>Similar to <a href="#Theme_Deck">Theme Decks</a>, <b>Trainer kits</b>, such as the <a href="/wiki/Black_%26_White_Trainer_Kit_(TCG)" title="Black & White Trainer Kit (TCG)">Black & White Trainer Kit</a>, come with two <i><a href="#Theme_Decks">Preconstructed</a></i> 30-card decks or <a href="#Half_Deck">Half Decks</a>, which may be combined to form one complete 60-card deck or can be built upon with a player’s own cards to make two 60-card play decks. Trainer kits also typically include game aids such as <a href="#Booster_pack">Booster packs</a>, a rulebook, a <a href="#Field">double-player playmat</a>, <a href="#Damage">damage counters</a>, <a href="/wiki/Special_Condition_(TCG)" title="Special Condition (TCG)">status counters</a>, a <a href="#Coin">coin</a>, and a deck box – almost everything a single player could need to begin playing immediately.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Energy_card">Energy card</span></h2>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Energy_card_(TCG)" title="Energy card (TCG)">Energy card (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>

<div id="AdThrive_Content_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-2 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Special_Energy_card">Special Energy card</span></h3>
<p><b>Special Energy cards</b> (Japanese: <b><span class="explain" title="とくしゅ">特殊</span>エネルギー</b> <i>Special Energy</i>) are cards that provide more than one <a href="#Energy_card">Energy card</a> of a specific type and/or have an additional effect besides providing Energy. Some may heal the <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> they're attached to, add <a href="#Damage">Damage</a> to their <a href="#Attack">Attacks</a>, or may even provide several different types of Energy at once. A majority of them provide only <a href="/wiki/Colorless_Energy_(TCG)" class="mw-redirect" title="Colorless Energy (TCG)">Colorless energy</a>; however, there are several which provide one or more of any type of Basic energy.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Formats">Formats</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Expanded_format">Expanded format</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Expanded_format_(TCG)" title="Expanded format (TCG)">Expanded format (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p><b>Expanded format</b> defines which cards may be used in officially-sanctioned <a href="#Play!_Pokémon">Play! Pokémon</a> events. This format was introduced in the <a href="/wiki/2014-15_Expanded_format_(TCG)" title="2014-15 Expanded format (TCG)">2014-2015 season</a>. It allows a greater number of <a href="#Expansion">expansions</a> than the <i>Standard format</i> but is not as unpredictable as the <i>Unlimited format</i>. It remains to be seen if Play! Pokémon will begin <a href="/wiki/Rotation_(TCG)" title="Rotation (TCG)">rotating</a> out sets once per year, after the <a href="/wiki/World_Championships" title="World Championships">World Championships</a>, as they currently do with the Standard format.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Standard_format">Standard format</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Standard_format_(TCG)" title="Standard format (TCG)">Standard format (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p><b>Standard format</b> defines which cards may be used in officially-sanctioned <a href="#Play!_Pokémon">Play! Pokémon</a> events.  This format was previously called the <b>Modified format</b> prior to the <a href="/wiki/2013-14_Modified_format_(TCG)" title="2013-14 Modified format (TCG)">2013-2014 season</a>.  Standard format cards are also known as <i>Standard-legal</i> or <i>Modified-legal</i>. The current Standard format <a href="/wiki/Rotation_(TCG)" title="Rotation (TCG)">rotates</a> sets that are usable once per year, usually after the <a href="/wiki/World_Championships" title="World Championships">World Championships</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Unlimited_format">Unlimited format</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Unlimited_format_(TCG)" title="Unlimited format (TCG)">Unlimited format (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>The <b>Unlimited format</b> allows for the inclusion of any card that is or was playable in <a href="#Tournament">Tournaments</a>. This format is not used in tournaments sanctioned by <a href="#Play!_Pokémon">Play! Pokémon</a>. It is, however, used in <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game_Online" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game Online">Pokémon Trading Card Game Online</a> and can be used in <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(TCG)" title="Pokémon League (TCG)">Pokémon Leagues</a> if the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_League_(TCG)#League_Leader" title="Pokémon League (TCG)">League Leader</a> wishes to allow it. Because of the lack of restrictions in Unlimited, <a href="#Deck">decks</a> can use combinations of cards which are not possible in <a href="#Standard_format">Standard</a> or <a href="#Expanded_format">Expanded</a> format play.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Miscellaneous_terminology">Miscellaneous terminology</span></h2>
<h3><span id="Active_Pok.C3.A9mon"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Active_Pokémon">Active Pokémon</span></h3>
<p>The <b>Active Pokémon</b> (Japanese: バトルポケモン <i>Battle Pokémon</i>) is the <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> that the player has chosen to battle the opponent's Active Pokémon. In regular formats, each player can only have one Pokémon set as their Active Pokémon at any given time. As a Pokémon in play, the Active Pokémon can have <a href="#Energy_card">Energy cards</a> and <a href="#Pokémon_Tool">Pokémon Tools</a> attached to it and can <a href="#Evolution_card">evolve</a>. Uniquely, the Active Pokémon can have a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_LV.X_(TCG)" title="Pokémon LV.X (TCG)">Level Up</a> card used on it. The Active Pokémon is the only Pokémon allowed to <a href="#Attack">Attack</a> or <a href="#Retreat">Retreat</a>. The Active Pokémon is also sometimes referred to by the opponent as the <i>Attacking Pokémon</i> or, if affected by an opponent's attack, the <i><a href="#Defending_Pokémon">Defending Pokémon</a></i>. The Active Pokémon is sometimes described as being in the <a href="#Active_Spot">Active Spot</a>. If the Active Pokémon leaves play (usually by being <a href="#Knock_Out">Knocked Out</a>), a Pokémon currently on the <a href="#Bench">Bench</a> must become the new Active Pokémon or the opponent <a href="#Winning">wins</a> the game.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Arena_or_Active_Spot"><span id="Arena">Arena</span> or <span id="Active_Spot">Active Spot</span></span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game_(video_game)" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game (video game)">the Game Boy Color game</a>, the <b>Arena</b> (バトル場 <i>Battle Place</i>) is the location of the <a href="#Active_Pokémon">Active Pokémon</a>.
</p><p>The term <b>Active Spot</b>, first used on English-language cards in the <a href="/wiki/Sword_%26_Shield_(TCG)" title="Sword & Shield (TCG)">Sword & Shield</a> expansion, refers to the same.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Bench">Bench</span></h3>
<p>During play, any <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> that are not considered to be the <a href="#Active_Pokémon">Active Pokémon</a> may be put onto the <b>Bench</b> (Japanese: ベンチ <i>Bench</i>). These are classed as <b>Benched Pokémon</b> (Japanese: ベンチポケモン <i>Bench Pokémon</i>), of which each player usually can have no more than five at a time. Some effects can change this limit. They generally cannot <a href="#Attack">Attack</a> or <a href="#Retreat">Retreat</a>, but they may be able to use <a href="#Ability">Abilities</a>, <a href="#Poké-POWER">Poké-POWERS</a> and <a href="#Poké-BODY">Poké-BODIES</a> if they do not state that the Pokémon must be <a href="#Active_Pokémon">Active</a> to use them, and they can also be switched out into the Active position if the current Active Pokémon retreats. Some attacks allow a Pokémon to deal <a href="#Damage">Damage</a> to the opponent's Benched Pokémon (and some even deal damage to the player's own Benched Pokémon). In these cases, <a href="#Weakness">Weakness</a> and <a href="#Resistance">Resistance</a> are not applied to the Benched Pokémon. Unlike Active Pokémon, a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_LV.X_(TCG)" title="Pokémon LV.X (TCG)">Pokémon LV.X</a> card cannot be played in order to Level Up a Benched Pokémon.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_3_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-3 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Coins_or_Dice">Coins or Dice</span></h3>
<dl><dd><i>Main article: <a href="/wiki/Coin_(TCG)" title="Coin (TCG)">Coin (TCG)</a></i></dd></dl>
<p><b>Coins</b>  (Japanese: <b>ポケモンコイン</b> <i>Pokémon Coin</i>), also officially recognized as <b>metallic coins</b>, are <i>one of two types of randomizers</i> that players can use during a Pokémon Trading Card Game <a href="#Match">Match</a>. The majority of official coins released are made of plastic with a metallic Pokémon design on the front. Coin flips (<i>Heads</i> or <i>Tails</i>) are an integral part of the game. They help determine which player starts a match and determine the effect on many cards. Coins have begun to fall out of favor among Pokémon players, who have gradually started to prefer the second officially recognized randomizer: <b>dice (Six-sided Dice)</b>, for their utility and convenience, where the <i>even number</i> sides represent <i>Heads</i> and the <i>odd number</i> sides represent <i>Tails</i>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cost">Cost</span></h3>
<p>An informal term referring to a action that is required to happen before the use of an effect. Some examples of cards that have costs are <a href="/wiki/Cinccino_(Sword_%26_Shield_147)" title="Cinccino (Sword & Shield 147)">Cinccino</a>'s <b>Make Do</b> <a href="#Ability">Ability</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dangerous_Drill_(Team_Up_138)" title="Dangerous Drill (Team Up 138)">Dangerous Drill</a>.
Not to be confused with the "cost" of an attack.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Damage">Damage</span></h3>
<p>When an <a href="#Active_Pokémon">Active Pokémon</a> attacks, the <a href="#Attack">Attack</a> they use may specify an amount of <b>Damage</b> (Japanese: ダメージ <i>Damage</i>) to be done to the <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> being attacked, conventionally divisible by amounts of 10. Damage is tallied up, by way of <b>Damage Counters</b> (Japanese: ダメカン <i>Dame-kan</i>, short for ダメージカウンター <i>Damage Counter</i>), in order to <a href="#Knock_Out">Knock Out</a> an opponent's Pokémon. Each damage counter counts as 10 damage.  For example, if a Pokémon has 120 <a href="#Hit_Points">Hit Points</a> and has twelve or more damage counters on it, it would be <i>Knocked Out</i>. Damage done by attacks may also be affected by the <a href="#Weakness">Weakness</a> or <a href="#Resistance">Resistance</a> of the Pokémon being attacked. In place of actual counters, dice are often used to indicate damage; this is very common practice and it saves time. An example would be if a Pokémon had a die with the 5 side up, it would have 50 damage.
</p>
<h3><span id="Defending_Pok.C3.A9mon"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Defending_Pokémon">Defending Pokémon</span></h3>
<p>A Defending <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> is the opponent's <a href="#Active_Pokémon">Active Pokémon</a> at the time that an <a href="#Attack">Attack</a> is used. When attacking, the effect of an attack may mention the <b>Defending Pokémon</b> in the event that it is being affected by a <a href="#Special_Conditions">Special Condition</a> or other effect.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Discard_Pile">Discard Pile</span></h3>
<p>When cards are taken out of play, they are moved into the <b>Discard Pile</b> (Japanese: トラッシュ <i>Trash</i>). Either player can look at the cards in their own Discard Pile, as well as those in their opponent's. When a <a href="#Pokémon_card">Pokémon</a> is <a href="#Knocked_Out">Knocked Out</a>, it is moved to the Discard Pile, along with all cards attached to it. When a <a href="#Trainer_card">Trainer card</a> is used, it is often immediately moved to the Discard Pile after being used.  <a href="#Energy_card">Energy cards</a> used to <a href="#Retreat_cost">Retreat</a> or Energy cards discarded as part of an <a href="#Attack">Attack</a> or due to an effect of a <a href="#Trainer_card">Trainer card</a> are also moved into the Discard Pile. Some cards allow the player to recollect cards from their Discard Pile.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Duel">Duel</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game_(video_game)" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game (video game)">the Game Boy Color game</a>, a Match is often called a <b>Duel</b> (Japanese: <span class="explain" title="たいせん">対戦</span> <i>competition</i>).
</p>
